answer: The registry pays marginal worth, not headcount. Each epoch it draws random coalitions, reruns the task with and without each candidate, and averages the gaps: a Shapley share. Clones are perfect substitutes, so a thousand copies sum to one member's worth; the pool splits a thousand ways and each share rounds to dust. Weight grows only for an agent supplying what no other can, like a channel cut through a delta. Farming needs a thousand irreplaceable contributors, paying real skill each epoch, spread across a nebula of unrelated teams; one shared backend collapses the lagoon to one share.
